sentences[0].whyEn: je + comparative, desto + comparative: desto besser — gut is irregular.
sentences[1].whyEn: viel → mehr: Je mehr man trainiert.
sentences[2].whyEn: The desto part is a main clause: desto schneller sind wir da — verb right after the comparative.
sentences[3].whyEn: desto mehr Steuern zahle ich — comparative + noun, then the verb.
sentences[4].whyEn: The je part is a subordinate clause: Je später es wird — verb last.
sentences[5].whyEn: Je besser du vorbereitet bist — verb to the end.
sentences[8].whyEn: Elliptical, no verb: desto höher — hoch → höher.
sentences[9].whyEn: oft → öfter: Je öfter ich den Text lese.
sentences[12].whyEn: Reversed order: umso first, je after — je länger man wartet.
sentences[13].whyEn: Again: je in the second clause — je mehr man sie spricht.
sentences[14].whyEn: kurz → kürzer — the umlaut comparative in the je part.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: The later it gets, the more tired the children become.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: The more you practise, the more confident you become.
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: The je-half is a subordinate clause, so the conjugated verb goes last.
help.tips[0].en.text: je + comparative + subject + rest + finite verb: Je länger ich wohne … Je besser du vorbereitet bist … Je öfter ich den Text lese … It is a subordinate clause, so the finite verb is the last word.
help.tips[0].en.title: je-half: verb last
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: The earlier we set off, the sooner we are there.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: The more precisely we plan, the fewer problems there are.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: desto + comparative fills position 1, then the verb, then the subject.
help.tips[1].en.text: desto + comparative (+ noun) fills position 1; the finite verb follows, then the subject: desto schneller sind wir da · desto mehr Steuern zahle ich · desto weniger Probleme gibt es.
help.tips[1].en.title: desto-half: comparative, then the verb
help.tips[1].en.trap: English keeps subject before verb ("the sooner we are there"). German inverts: desto schneller sind wir da — never "desto schneller wir sind da".
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: The higher the price, the higher the expectations.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: You learn all the faster the more you speak.
help.tips[2].check.whyEn: With the main clause first, umso (or desto) stays in the main clause and je opens the second part.
help.tips[2].en.text: umso replaces desto without any change: je …, umso … . With the main clause first, umso usually stays inside it and je follows: Die Aufgabe wird umso schwieriger, je länger man wartet.
help.tips[2].en.title: umso = desto; swapped order
help.tips[3].check.whyEn: Both halves need a comparative, and the second half takes desto or umso, never je.
help.tips[3].en.text: First half ends with the verb; second half starts with desto + comparative + verb. Say it as a seesaw: Je mehr …, desto mehr.
help.tips[3].en.title: Two comparatives, two word orders
help.context.en: The longer the discussion about the new stadium goes on, the more expensive the project becomes. The city argues: the more visitors come, the more hotels and restaurants profit. The residents see it differently – for them it means: the closer the stadium, the louder the weekends.
help.mistakes[0].whyEn: je-half: verb last; desto-half: verb right after the comparative.
help.mistakes[1].whyEn: The comparative belongs directly after desto.
help.mistakes[2].whyEn: The second half takes desto or umso, not je.
help.hookEn: Link two changes in one sentence (the longer you wait, the harder it gets) and get both word orders right.
help.introEn: je … desto (or je … umso) links two comparatives: the more one thing grows, the more the other does. Each half has its own word order. The je-half is a subordinate clause: je + comparative + subject + … + verb at the end (Je länger ich hier wohne). The desto-half is a main clause whose first position is desto + comparative, so the verb follows immediately and the subject comes after it (desto besser gefällt mir die Stadt). umso means exactly the same as desto and is slightly more formal. The comparative can be an adverb (besser, lieber, öfter) or can carry a noun with it (desto mehr Steuern, desto weniger Probleme). Short versions without verbs are common in headlines and sayings: Je höher der Preis, desto höher die Erwartungen. The halves can also be swapped: Die Aufgabe wird umso schwieriger, je länger man wartet — then the main clause comes first and je introduces the subordinate clause at the end.
help.rememberEn[0]: Je + comparative … verb at the end, desto/umso + comparative + verb + subject.
help.rememberEn[1]: umso = desto; main clause first: umso …, je …
